**Layer groups.** Let $\rho: G \to \mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be the projection to the plane action. The kernel of $\rho$ has order at most 2 and is central.

- If $\rho$ is injective, $G \cong \rho(G)$, which is a wallpaper group $W$.
- If the kernel is $\langle\sigma_h\rangle$, the map $(\rho,\varepsilon): G \to W \times \{\pm1\}$ is injective with image $W \times \{\pm1\}$, so $G \cong W \times \mathbb{Z}_2$.

So every layer group is abstractly isomorphic to some $W$ or $W \times \mathbb{Z}_2$, which gives at most $17 + 17 = 34$ classes. All 34 occur, and they are pairwise distinct: wallpaper groups are pairwise non-isomorphic, $W \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ has a nontrivial finite normal subgroup while $W$ does not, and quotienting $W_1 \times \mathbb{Z}_2 \cong W_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ by its maximal finite normal subgroup would force $W_1 \cong W_2$. So the layer count is 34.

This rules out Solutions 2 and 3, which give 68 and 63 layer classes, both above the upper bound of 34.

**Rod groups.** Each rod group is virtually $\mathbb{Z}$, so it is either $F \rtimes_\alpha \mathbb{Z}$ (quotient $\mathbb{Z}$) or an amalgam $A *_F B$ with $[A:F]=[B:F]=2$ (quotient $D_\infty$). I checked the structure of Solution 1's enumeration, including the $p\bar4$ case with $F=\mathbb{Z}_2$, the $\mathrm{Aut}$-conjugacy reductions, and the amalgam identifications, and found them consistent. I did not verify all 75 groups individually, so the rod count of 32 is plausible but not confirmed.

Solution 1 is the only candidate consistent with the layer bound, and its layer count is correct. Its rod count is unverified but reasonable.

CHOICE: 1
